summary: The open-cell chart has Jacobian 𝗀(Z)^{k−1} times two Cayley densities; Haar.lintegral_chart_rotate_le bounds the chart integral by the Haar integral; the hypothesis is the chart integral in Cayley coordinates.

steps.claim: Take the measure-preserving coordinates e and the Jacobian formula of openCellChart.

steps.lean:
(Haar.lintegral_chart_rotate_le e he
  (isOpen_openCell.measurableSet.prod .univ) (@openCellChart_injOn 𝔰) h_jac).exists.elim fun t e ↦
    by
steps.claim: Since openCellChart is injective on Ω × (all parameters) and differentiable there with Jacobian w(p) = 𝗀(Z)^{k−1}·cayleyDensity(1, skewColumnEquiv(θ, 0))·cayleyDensity(1, η), there is a real t with ∫_{Ω×…} (w(p)/vol U(r))·f(e^{it}·openCellChart(p)) dp ≤ ∫_{G₁(𝔰)} f(e^{it}…)… ≤ the Haar integral.

steps.lean:
grw [← lintegral_mul_left_eq_self f (circleScalar t)⁻¹, ← e, ← one_mul L,
    ← (by simpa [cayleyDenom] using (lintegral_cayleyDensity_skewColumnEquiv 𝔰.k₀ 0 one_pos) :),
    ← lintegral_mul_const, h (cayleyChart 1 (skewColumnEquiv _ (‹_›, 0)))]
steps.claim: Use ∫ f = ∫ f(e^{−it}·) (left invariance), write L = 1·L with 1 = the integral over θ of the normalized Cayley density at η = 0 (lintegral_cayleyDensity_skewColumnEquiv, cayleyDensity(1, 0) = 1), and apply h with k = cayleyChart(1, skewColumnEquiv(k₀)(θ, 0)): it suffices to compare the resulting iterated integrals.

steps.lean:
simp (disch := first | finiteness | with_unfolding_all fun_prop) [volume_eq_prod _ (_ × _),
    openCellChart, ← prod_restrict, lintegral_prod, @lintegral_prod_symm 𝔰.UnipotentParams,
    lintegral_eq_cayleyChart, besselHaar₀, volU,
    lintegral_map, ← lintegral_const_mul, ← mul_assoc, ← ofReal_mul, ← ofReal_mul', openCellConst]
steps.claim: Expand: the chart integral is an iterated integral over Z ∈ Ω, θ, q, η, r (Fubini on the product of the parameter spaces); the U(κ) Haar integrals are written in Cayley coordinates (lintegral_eq_cayleyChart) and the 𝖴⁰ integrals through besselHaar₀; the constants combine into c_G(𝔰) (vol U(k), vol U(r), sphereDensity(k, 1)).
Exchange two integrations and compare the integrands pointwise; the remaining factors agree.
